what: After the user merges a girihelix PR, clean up in this order: `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only`, delete the local branch with `git branch -d`, then `git fetch --prune origin`. GitHub may have already auto-deleted the remote branch, in which case `git push origin --delete` fails with "remote ref does not exist" and the prune removes the stale `origin/<branch>` tracking ref instead.
why: The remote branch is often already gone on merge, so treating the delete failure as an error wastes a turn; the prune is the actual step needed.
